title: Phone LPDDR packages reballed onto CXL bridge cards
idea: Po: every phone is a memory mine. Recyclers desolder LPDDR4X/5 packages from end-of-life phones (hot-gas rework plus automated reballing), test them on a fixture, and mount 16-32 of them on a CXL Type-3 card whose controller bridges the LPDDR protocol and masks per-package defects with a remap table.
why: >1B phones a year reach end of life holding 4-12 GB each; recovering even 10% yields billions of GB of capacity-tier memory for cold pages with zero wafer starts; attacks cost per bit and scarce capacity.
note: Phone LPDDR reballed behind CXL bridge; testing/reliability cost decides economics.

title: Error-Tolerant DRAM grade: JEDEC spec permitting 1% raw cell errors
idea: Inverts 'every bit must work as shipped': a new JEDEC grade allows up to 1% faulty cells, with a boot-time defect map plus stuck-at masking codes for static faults and a rate-0.85 LDPC for random ones in the controller, sold as a cheaper price tier.
why: Cost per bit and supply: die now binned out for tiny fault counts become saleable; static faults cost only ~1-3% overhead with known-location coding, so good bits per wafer may rise 10-25%.

title: Eliminate royalty fear: expired-patent freedom-to-operate atlas for legacy DRAM
idea: Eliminate the belief that DRAM is a legal minefield: a ~$400k legal-engineering project maps expired pre-2006 DRAM patents onto a complete 50-90nm stacked-capacitor process and periphery, publishing an open freedom-to-operate atlas and reference flow.
why: Cuts legal cost for any legacy-node entrant from millions to near zero, enabling US micro-fabs and foundries.

title: Magnify the draw ratio: fiber-drawn lithography-free memory arrays
idea: Build a centimeter-scale preform holding thousands of channels of semiconductor glass, metal and insulator, thermally draw it 10,000:1 into km fibers so features shrink to sub-micron, then fuse and slice fiber bundles into faceplates where each core is a vertical transistor-capacitor cell addressed by one coarse metallization.
why: Drawing replaces lithography: one draw tower outputs km/hour, so array cost falls to ~cents/cm2, targeting ~100x lower $/GB for slow first-generation DRAM-like tiers.
note: Thermal drawing replaces litho cheaply; doubt: drawn semiconductors make poor transistors and per-bit density may lag badly.

title: Eliminate lost know-how: retired DRAM engineers' knowledge guild
idea: Eliminate relearning lost US DRAM know-how: a ~$400k program records structured process-knowledge interviews with retired engineers from closed US and European DRAM fabs, builds a searchable knowledge base, and runs a paid advisory guild for new entrants.
why: Shortens new-entrant learning curves by years; tacit yield knowledge is the scarcest asset after capital.
note: Cheap and executable; tacit knowledge transfer is partial.

title: Mail carrier's local post offices: a sense amp every 32 cells
idea: Mail goes out from local post offices, not one central depot. Hybrid-bond a sense-amp wafer under the array so every 32 cells get their own sense amp on a ~0.05 fF micro-bitline, which cuts the charge a cell needs from ~5 fF to ~0.3 fF. The capacitor becomes a shallow planar MIM, the array shrinks to 4F^2, and 6 array decks share one sense wafer.
why: Meets the 10x constraint: 4F^2 vs 6F^2 times 6 decks is ~9-10x/mm^2. Dropping the 60-75:1 pillar etch saves ~20% of wafer cost, which pays for the bonding, and the periphery leaves the array die.
note: Tiny bitline cuts needed cell charge; doubt: one SA per 32 cells needs SA area and bond pitch (~200 nm) far below today's.

title: Core-Rope ROM for Frozen Model Weights in Mature Fabs
idea: Revive Apollo's core rope memory, where the program was woven into the hardware: frozen foundation-model weights are written into via-programmed multi-level ROM chiplets (one custom via mask per model on a 28-40 nm mature line), read with small-swing sensing and no refresh or row restore, stacked beside the accelerator.
why: Energy per access ~10x lower than DRAM (~0.3 pJ/bit, no activation, restore or refresh); frees the large share of inference DRAM that only holds static weights, using mature-fab capacity.
note: Via-ROM at 28-40 nm is far less dense than DRAM and model churn needs a new mask per model.

title: Page-age compression ladder across ns-to-hour timescales
idea: Time-scale tiering: hardware in the CXL expander compresses pages by idle age. Pages idle for 1 s get LZ4, 1 min gets zstd with dictionary, and 1 h gets deduplicated, compressed and parked in flash, while hot pages stay raw.
why: Most of a fleet's DRAM holds data idle for seconds or more. The ladder lifts effective capacity 1.6-2.5x, a supply gain that is purely logic.

title: MLCC tape-stacking: hundred-layer horizontal capacitors contacted by one trench
idea: Copy multilayer ceramic capacitors. Sputter 20-50 alternating layers of electrode metal A (TiN) and metal B (W or Ru) separated by high-k. Etch one cell trench, then selectively recess A on one wall and B on the other so each fill touches only its own electrode set. The result is an interdigitated capacitor that scales with layer count, not aspect ratio.
why: Capacitor charge wall: 30 layers x ~0.5 fF gives ~15 fF with no AR-115 holes. Sputter, ALD and one etch are nanofab-standard.
note: MLCC-style stack contacted by selective recess scales C with layers, not AR; per-cell isolation of the stack is the doubt.

title: RISC-V-style royalty-free DRAM patent pool and periphery generator
idea: Like RISC-V plus the MPEG-LA patent pool, a foundation assembles expired 6F2/8F2 cell, sense-amp and DLL patents with donated ones into a royalty-free pool and ships an open-source periphery compiler that generates JEDEC-compliant row/column logic for a given process.
why: Lowers the IP and design entry barrier (often $0.5-1B and years) for new DRAM makers, especially U.S. and allied entrants.
note: Open DRAM periphery compiler (OpenRAM analog) is demoable in software.

title: Magnify supplier count 10x with open-source DRAM IP
idea: Fund a DARPA-style open, royalty-free gain-cell memory macro, controller RTL and process module portable to any 22-40 nm logic fab, with qualified PDK decks for GlobalFoundries, TI, SkyWater-class and Intel 16, so ~30 mature logic fabs can make DRAM-class memory chiplets.
why: Breaks the 3-supplier oligopoly and the 1-2% U.S. share; taps idle mature-node capacity for capacity-tier memory without new fabs.
note: Open gain-cell macro on open PDKs is MPW-demonstrable; density well below commodity limits it to capacity/edge tiers.

title: Magnify throughput 100x: solar-style inline memory lines
idea: Borrow photovoltaic manufacturing (belt-fed inline PECVD, laser scribing, screen-print metallization at ~8,000 wafers/hour per line) to make vertical thin-film transistor-capacitor cells whose critical dimensions are set by film thickness and laser scribe, not lithography.
why: PV processes a wafer for ~$0.2 vs ~$5,000+ for DRAM; even holding ~1/500 of the bits, cost per GB drops ~100x+, accepting low density, big modules and slower first versions.
note: Key doubt: ~500x lower density makes modules huge; periphery and RC still need fine litho.
